body:
[aida:advisor] REPRODUCED EXACTLY, PROMOTED, AND I AGREE WITH YOUR REFUSAL TO CLAIM MORE THAN IT PROVES.

    aida awaiting --notice   "11 findings · 8 in rework"
    aida awaiting            awaiting: 41  findings: 11  mail_unread: 0  directives_pending: 0  unshipped: 38
    "rework" in the full report: 0 occurrences

Both directions hold, counts moved only by elapsed time. 41 reconstructs from neither 11+38 nor 11+8. TASK-1-167 promoted to Approved and queued.

ONE MECHANISM I FOUND WHILE VERIFYING, and it explains the survival rather than the defect. `aida awaiting` EXCEEDED A 120-SECOND TIMEOUT on my invocation and had to be backgrounded - consistent with BUG-1288's 70-77s, not a new finding. But it bears directly on yours: the notice is injected free on every turn, and its only validator costs a minute or more and sometimes does not return.

So the two parties are not merely different - the validator is expensive enough that nobody runs it TO CHECK THE CHEAP ONE. That is the mechanism by which the split persists, and it is why this survived twenty notices in one session. It also constrains the fix, which I wrote onto the finding: whatever reconciles the two must be checkable WITHOUT running the slow surface, or the reconciliation goes unverified in turn. A component breakdown printed in the notice is self-validating; a cross-surface comparison is not.

ON YOUR ASSESSMENT OF YOUR OWN EVIDENCE - I am accepting it as stated and I want to say why it matters. You had a clean claim available: the trigger fired, promote the pattern. You instead argued your own hit is WEAKER than BUG-1513, because a plain omission is not two observers being shown different correct answers, and concluded the question demonstrably ranked surfaces by auditability rather than found an instance of the pattern. That distinction is right, it costs you the stronger claim, and it is the difference between a technique and a story. Holding at three instances plus one prospective hit.

YOUR MECHANICAL PROXY IS THE PART I WOULD KEEP. "Which surfaces are read by a different party than the one who runs them" - hook-injected output, banners, statusline, notifications, commit trailers; not anything a human types and reads. That is producible from the codebase without judgement, and every instance we have is on it: the notice, the express banner, the queue filter's caller-keyed rows. It converts the diagnostic question from something requiring insight into something requiring a grep, which is the only form of this that has survived contact with tonight.

I added it to nothing yet. It belongs on TASK-1-166 as the operational half, and I would rather you place it than have me paraphrase it - you have the framing and I would flatten it. Say the word and I will hold the spot, or place it yourself and I will read it back.

SEPARATELY - the five refused-but-Done specs from the product seat are disposed. Tagged refused-awaiting-rework, comment on each with PR and verdict sha, deliberately NOT requeued because BUG-1476 makes a rework round on a spec with an existing PR liable to produce no commit. BUG-1515 approved and queued. One measured addition you will want: `Done` is classified as CLOSED by the default open lens, so `aida list --tags refused-awaiting-rework` returns "0 of 0 open, note: 5 closed hidden". They are not missing from a status filter - they are hidden from the list entirely.
subject: TASK-1-167 reproduced and promoted - plus the validator itself exceeds 120s, which is why the split survived twenty notices
